key_insight: This paper introduces an "Embodied World Model Evaluation Turing Test": a human-centered, comprehensive protocol that measures whether video foundation models produce perceptually convincing and robust predictions for embodied AI. It exposes gaps between automated metrics and human judgment and provides standardized robustness checks for generative world models.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a standardized, human-anchored evaluation for generative predictive world models in Embodied AI—current automated metrics often fail to capture perceptual fidelity and robustness needed for downstream embodied tasks.
method: Turing-test style human evaluation: present human raters with real vs. model-predicted video sequences from embodied scenarios and collect perceptual judgments.
Diverse scenario and stress-test suite: curated embodied tasks and targeted perturbations (e.g., long horizons, occlusion, interaction changes) to probe generative generalization and robustness.
Combined analysis: aggregate human preferences with automated metrics and failure-mode diagnostics to rank models and surface specific weaknesses for improvement.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a standardized, human-grounded benchmark to evaluate and diagnose video-based world models, enabling better model selection and targeted improvements that align with human perception and robustness requirements.
visual_elements: Turing-test protocol flowchart showing stimulus generation, human judgment, and scoring pipeline.
Side-by-side examples (real vs predicted) with human preference percentages to illustrate perceptual differences.
Robustness heatmap/grid comparing model performance across perturbations (occlusion, horizon length, interaction) and tasks.
Radar/spider chart summarizing per-model strengths and failure modes (fidelity, temporal consistency, interaction plausibility, robustness).
paper_title: Wow, wo, val! A Comprehensive Embodied World Model Evaluation Turing Test
paper_authors: Chun-Kai Fan, Xiaowei Chi, Xiaozhu Ju, Hao Li, Yong Bao
